H1.claim: within the adjudicating grid, pointer-stable has a lower p95 TTFT per turn than transcript-grow
H1.interval: percentile bootstrap inside quantile_ci, resamples=10000, seed=20261020, two-sided LEVEL=0.95, clamped to bracket the point (:238), printed via render_estimate (:467)
H1.admissibility: n >= MIN_N(20) AND n*(1-q) >= TAIL_MIN(3) enforced at :223; at q=0.95 that is n >= 60 (min_n_for :167). n=48 (RUN-C-V2 grid) is refused, not caveated
H1.ranking_rule: disjoint 95% bootstrap intervals: C.hi < A.lo; no paired quantile test exists in analyze_stats, so overlapping intervals mean NO ranking claim
H1.on_missing_n: quantile_ci raises InsufficientSamples / analyze records 'refused' (:550); H1 is then not adjudicable, the refusal message is quoted verbatim, and the threshold is never lowered; nearest-rank p95 from analyze_longrun.py is not admissible
H1.recorded_p95_disagreement: 838.85/356.12 ms interpolated (analysis.txt) vs 840.4/371.7 ms nearest-rank (PER-ARM TABLE in the same file); PARM-1 binds the analyze_stats.quantile_ci number only

H2.claim: within the same grid, pointer-stable carries fewer total prompt tokens per completed turn than transcript-grow
H2.unit_of_account: prompt_tokens summed over non-excluded completed turns, divided by that same count; not wall time, not request count (identical by construction), not completion tokens as primary
H2.materiality_margin: C per-turn total <= 0.95 x A (5% reduction) on prompt_tokens AND < 1.00 x on uncached
H2.margin_rationale: prompt tokens are deterministic for fixed (fixture, arm, turn); a win must not rest on a rounding-level difference. 5% is a declared design choice, not a measurement
H2.why_primary: the pointer mechanism is not re-sending history; if carried prompt work does not fall, a p95 win is a serving artefact, not the thesis

card_premise_disagreement.stated_in_brief: RUN-C-V2 recorded pointer-stable with the higher total prompt tokens
card_premise_disagreement.status: NOT REPRODUCED (v2/v4 fixtures, 3 checkpoint items, no v6 rows); not refuted either - H2 stays primary because v6 prompt composition is where C's constant prefix could stop dominating

H3.claim: pointer-stable is no worse than transcript-grow on checkpoint accuracy over the decidable denominator by more than the stated margin
H3.population: grade_v5.py cells only, via analyze_stats.accuracy_from_grade(grade, arm) :431-463; row-derived denominators forbidden (v6 rows carry answer_kind=null)
H3.denominator: decidable = pass + fail; undecidable (verdict text) and missing (reason == turn_missing) leave the denominator and are printed by name
H3.margin_rationale: at 12 items exact two-sided McNemar reaches only p=0.0386 at a 10-2 split (docs/CHECKPOINT-COVERAGE.md §4), so a p-value-shaped margin would license a 3-checkpoint loss at some splits and refuse it at others
H3.secondary_veto: if b+c >= 6 (mcnemar_exact :295) and exact two-sided p < 0.05 with c = C-right/A-wrong, H3 fails regardless of margin; below 6 discordant pairs the test is refused and only the fixed margin decides
H3.veto: a quality failure vetoes a latency win; equal-or-better quality is a gate on every other result, not a footnote
H3.unadjudicable_clause: if either arm's decidable < 8 of 12, H3 returns no verdict and the run is not adjudicable; never read as pass

decision_matrix.wording: pointer-stable beats transcript-grow on p95 TTFT (C hi < A lo) and on total prompt work per completed turn, with quality no worse than 2 of 12 checkpoints. The operator's three-part claim holds in this grid.

Latency and work both favour pointer-stable, but the quality gate fails by more than 2 of 12 checkpoints (or a licensed McNemar finds it worse). Equal-or-better quality is a gate, so no win is claimed; the thesis is not supported.

Total prompt work is lower for pointer-stable but p95 TTFT is not distinguished (intervals overlap or the p95 was refused at n<60). Work alone does not satisfy the claim; the thesis as stated is not supported.

In the adjudicating grid pointer-stable shows neither a p95 TTFT win nor a total-work win while quality holds. The thesis is dead: the pointer design does not pay on either cost axis, and the quality result removes quality as the explanation.

decision_matrix.verdict: THE THESIS IS DEAD (with a quality regression)
decision_matrix.wording: Neither cost axis favours pointer-stable and its quality is worse by more than 2 of 12 checkpoints. The thesis is dead and the arm is additionally unacceptable on quality.
A p95 TTFT win is recorded, but total prompt work is not lower and quality fails. The win is a serving artefact; the thesis is not supported.
Work is lower, but p95 TTFT is not distinguished and quality fails. The thesis is not supported.
